name: SecretOnce
doc:
SecretOnce is the card that shows a freshly issued key: the value, a way to
copy it, and the sentence that has to be there — this is the only time it
appears.

The copy button is the one piece of script here, and it degrades to nothing:
without it the value is still selectable text in a field somebody can copy
by hand. What is never done is offering to show it again — the application
cannot, because only the hash was stored, and a screen that implies
otherwise teaches the wrong lesson about its own keys.
summary: SecretOnce is the card that shows a freshly issued key: the value, a way to copy it, and the sentence that has to be there — this is the only time it appears.

name: APIKeyRow
doc:
APIKeyRow is one line of the table. It is a plain struct and not an
auth.Key because ui does not import auth — the kit draws, and what it draws
is data. The application maps one to the other in three lines, and that
mapping is where "what a screen shows" is decided.
summary: APIKeyRow is one line of the table.

fields.name: Handle
fields.doc: Handle identifies the key without opening the hash.

name: APIKeysOpts
doc: APIKeysOpts is what the table can do besides list.
summary: APIKeysOpts is what the table can do besides list.

fields.name: Revoke
fields.doc: Revoke is where the revoke button posts, with the id in "id".

fields.name: CSRF
fields.doc: CSRF is the hidden token field, and a form that revokes a key has to carry one: pass trilha.CSRFInput(c).

fields.name: Empty
fields.doc: Empty replaces the default empty state.

name: APIKeysTable
doc:
APIKeysTable lists the keys of an application: what each one is called, what
it may do, when it was made and when it was last used.

The key itself is not here and cannot be — only the handle, which is the half
that identifies it without opening the hash. Revoking posts with a
confirmation, because it is the one action on this screen nobody can undo.
summary: APIKeysTable lists the keys of an application: what each one is called, what it may do, when it was made and when it was last used.
example:
return ui.APIKeysTable(c, linhas, ui.APIKeysOpts{Revoke: "/chaves/revogar"})


see: ui.SecretOnce

name: AuditOpts
doc:
AuditOpts is the screen around the trail: how much of it there is, what can
be filtered, and where the export lives.
summary: AuditOpts is the screen around the trail: how much of it there is, what can be filtered, and where the export lives.

fields.name: Params
fields.doc: Params is what Bind read from the query — the same ListParams the listing of any other screen uses, so ordering and paging are in the address and the back button works.

fields.name: Total
fields.doc: Total is how many records the filter matched, for the pagination.

fields.name: ID
fields.doc: ID is the fragment the table swaps into; empty uses "auditoria".

fields.name: Actions
fields.doc: Actions fills the action filter.

fields.name: Action
fields.doc: Action is the one currently chosen, so the select comes back on the option that is filtering.

fields.name: Export
fields.doc: Export is the address that downloads this same selection as a spreadsheet — a route answering with Ctx.CSV.

fields.name: Empty
fields.doc: Empty replaces the default empty state.

name: AuditTable
doc:
AuditTable is the screen every application with c.Audit ends up writing by
hand: who did what, to what, when and from where.

It is a DataTable underneath, which is the point: the filter form, the
ordering links, the pagination and the fragment swap are the ones every
other listing already has, and a trail that behaved differently from the
rest of the app would be a second thing to learn.
Reading the records is the application's job. Config.AuditSink is a write
interface with one method, and it stays that way: the framework has no
database, and the query behind this screen — a period, an actor, a table
this app chose — is not something it could write.
Fields is a detail and not a column. Each action carries its own keys, so a
column per key is a table that grows a column every time somebody audits
something new.
summary: AuditTable is the screen every application with c.Audit ends up writing by hand: who did what, to what, when and from where.

name: Datum
summary: Datum is one labelled value of a chart.

fields.name: Text
fields.doc: Text is the value as a person reads it — "R$ 1.204,50", "38 %", "1.2k".

name: Stat
doc:
Stat is the counter of a dashboard: a label, a value and an optional hint.
The value arrives already formatted — the framework has no locale, and the
app is the one that knows whether a thousand is 1,204 or 1.204.
summary: Stat is the counter of a dashboard: a label, a value and an optional hint.
example: ui.Stat("Documents", "1.204", ui.StatHint("+38 this week"))

name: StatHint
doc: StatHint is the second line of a Stat: a variation, a period, a total.
summary: StatHint is the second line of a Stat: a variation, a period, a total.

name: ChartTitle
doc:
ChartTitle names a chart for whoever cannot see it. With a title the drawing
is an image with a name (role="img" plus <title>); without one the drawing is
decoration (aria-hidden) and the table beside it — hidden from the eye, not
from the reader — is what says the numbers.
summary: ChartTitle names a chart for whoever cannot see it.

name: Bars
doc:
Bars draws one horizontal bar per Datum, proportional to the largest value,
with the label to the left and the value at the end of the bar. It is the
`<div style="width:37%">` of every dashboard, with the numbers still readable
when the CSS does not arrive.

A negative value draws no bar and keeps its label; a series whose largest
value is zero or less draws every bar empty.
summary: Bars draws one horizontal bar per Datum, proportional to the largest value, with the label to the left and the value at the end of the bar.

name: SparkOpts
doc:
SparkOpts is the size of a Sparkline in the same units its points are drawn
in; zero means 120 by 32.
summary: SparkOpts is the size of a Sparkline in the same units its points are drawn in; zero means 120 by 32.

name: Sparkline
doc:
Sparkline draws the series as one line, with no axis and no scale — the
shape of the last few weeks inside a Stat, not a chart to read values off.

One point alone, or a series where every value is the same, is a straight
line through the middle; an empty series draws nothing.
summary: Sparkline draws the series as one line, with no axis and no scale — the shape of the last few weeks inside a Stat, not a chart to read values off.
example: ui.Stat("Signups", "1,204", ui.Sparkline(weekly, ui.SparkOpts{}))

name: SparklineTitle
doc:
SparklineTitle is Sparkline with a name and the numbers in a hidden table,
for a line that stands on its own instead of inside a Stat.
summary: SparklineTitle is Sparkline with a name and the numbers in a hidden table, for a line that stands on its own instead of inside a Stat.
example: ui.SparklineTitle(weekly, ui.SparkOpts{Width: 240}, ui.ChartTitle("Signups per week"))

name: Donut
doc:
Donut draws the share of each Datum in the total as a ring, with the legend
as a list beside the drawing and not inside the SVG — a legend is text, and
text inside an SVG neither wraps nor is selected.

The ring is drawn with a dashed circle instead of arcs: no trigonometry, so
the same series always writes the same file. Negative values are ignored and
a total of zero draws the empty track.
summary: Donut draws the share of each Datum in the total as a ring, with the legend as a list beside the drawing and not inside the SVG — a legend is text, and text inside an SVG neither wraps nor is selected.

name: ChatMessage
doc:
ChatMessage is one turn already on the page. The assistant's text is
Markdown and goes through Markdown; the visitor's is plain text and stays
plain text — what someone typed is never markup.
summary: ChatMessage is one turn already on the page.

fields.name: Role
fields.doc: Role is "user" or "assistant".

name: ChatOpts
doc:
ChatOpts describes the conversation. Action is the only field that has to
be filled in.
summary: ChatOpts describes the conversation.

fields.name: ID
fields.doc: ID is the element id, and the prefix of the ids inside it.

fields.name: Action
fields.doc: Action is the route that answers, the one running ai.Serve.

fields.name: History
fields.doc: History is what was said before, oldest first.

fields.name: Greeting
fields.doc: Greeting is the Markdown shown when the history is empty.

fields.name: Placeholder
fields.doc: Placeholder, Submit and Label are the words on the screen.

fields.name: MaxLength
fields.doc: MaxLength caps the field.

fields.name: Steps
fields.doc: Steps shows what the agent did — the tool it called and what came back.

fields.name: Markdown
fields.doc: Markdown is how the answers are rendered.

name: Chat
doc:
Chat renders a conversation with an agent: the messages, the field and the
button. The route on the other side is ai.Serve.

With the script, the answer arrives word by word and the Markdown is
rendered when the message ends. Without it the form still submits: the
route answers the whole thing at once, and the page comes back with the
answer in the history. Nothing on the screen depends on the script running.
summary: Chat renders a conversation with an agent: the messages, the field and the button.
example:
ui.Chat(c, ui.ChatOpts{Action: "/api/chat", History: msgs})
ui.ChatScript(c)

name: ChatScript
doc:
ChatScript loads ui.chat.js, the behavior behind Chat: it sends the message,
reads the events and renders the answer as it arrives. Put it once, in the
layout of the area with the chat — Head does not load it, so a page without
a chat does not download it.
summary: ChatScript loads ui.chat.js, the behavior behind Chat: it sends the message, reads the events and renders the answer as it arrives.

name: ChatHTML
doc:
ChatHTML renders one answer the way Chat renders the history. It is the
adapter for ai.ServeOpts.HTML:

The done event then carries the rendered answer and the bubble stops being
plain text. The HTML is this package's — escaped by construction — which is
why handing it to the browser as HTML is safe and handing over a string from
anywhere else is not.
summary: ChatHTML renders one answer the way Chat renders the history.
example: ai.ServeOpts{HTML: ui.ChatHTML}.Serve(c, client, agent)

name: ComboboxOpts
doc:
ComboboxOpts describes the field. Name is the name the form posts and the
key of its message; Value and Label are what is already chosen — the value
the app stores and the text a person reads — so a form that came back with
messages comes back showing the choice instead of an identifier.
summary: ComboboxOpts describes the field.

fields.name: Source
fields.doc: Source is a GET route that answers ui.ComboboxOptions for ?q=.

fields.name: Options
fields.doc: Options is a short list, filtered without a round trip.

fields.name: With
fields.doc: With names other fields of the same form whose values travel with the search (?q=…&uf=SP), which is what makes a dependent picker stop being twenty lines of JavaScript in the app.

fields.name: MinChars
fields.doc: MinChars is how much has to be typed before the first search (1 when zero); Debounce is how long the field waits for the typing to stop (250ms when zero).

fields.name: Placeholder
fields.doc: Placeholder, Required and Attrs go on the text input.

name: Combobox
doc:
Combobox is a text field that searches: the server does the searching and
answers a list of options, the browser only shows it. It is the picker of a
classification among hundreds, of a city among thousands.

The value the form posts is the hidden input, so the app reads Name as any
other field. With this script off, or before anything was picked, the hidden
input is empty and what the person typed arrives as Name+"_q" — the route
resolves that text or answers 422, and the Label brings the field back the
way it was.
summary: Combobox is a text field that searches: the server does the searching and answers a list of options, the browser only shows it.

name: ComboboxOptions
signature: ComboboxOptions[T any](items []T, of func(T) (value, label string)) h.Node
doc:
ComboboxOptions is the answer of a search route: the options themselves, as
HTML, because the browser has nothing to decide about them.
summary: ComboboxOptions is the answer of a search route: the options themselves, as HTML, because the browser has nothing to decide about them.

name: CSVErrorsOpts
doc:
CSVErrorsOpts is what the list of rejected cells says. The zero value is a
sensible screen.
summary: CSVErrorsOpts is what the list of rejected cells says.

fields.name: Title
fields.doc: Title is the sentence above the table.

fields.name: Limit
fields.doc: Limit is how many cells are listed.

fields.name: Action
fields.doc: Action is what comes after the table — "Choose another file", usually.

name: CSVErrors
doc:
CSVErrors renders what BindCSV rejected, by line and column.

It exists because the alternative is what every import screen actually
shows — "error in the file" — which leaves somebody to find one bad date in
four thousand rows by eye. Line is numbered the way their editor numbers it,
with the header as line 1, and Column is the heading as it appears in the
file, so both halves of the message can be searched for.
Warnings are listed under the errors and read differently on purpose: a
column nobody claimed did not stop the import.
summary: CSVErrors renders what BindCSV rejected, by line and column.

name: DeferOpts
doc:
DeferOpts is what stands in the hole until the slow part arrives, and what
is said when it never does. The zero value is a skeleton and the kit's own
sentences.
summary: DeferOpts is what stands in the hole until the slow part arrives, and what is said when it never does.

fields.name: Placeholder
fields.doc: Placeholder is what is drawn while the fragment is on its way.

fields.name: Height
fields.doc: Height is how tall that skeleton is — "12rem".

fields.name: Then
fields.doc: Then is what the fragment does after it has arrived — Poll("30s", src) to keep watching.

fields.name: Load
fields.doc: Load is the label of the link a visitor without JavaScript sees.

fields.name: Error
fields.doc: Error and Retry are the two sentences of the failure: what happened, and the button that asks again.

fields.name: Retry
fields.doc: Error and Retry are the two sentences of the failure: what happened, and the button that asks again.

name: Defer
signature: Defer(c *trilha.Ctx, id, src string, opts ...DeferOpts) h.Node
doc:
Defer serves the page now and fills this part of it a moment later.

The dashboard that needs seven queries to draw does not have to hold the
whole page for the one that takes two seconds. The fast part is rendered on
the server as usual; this one is a placeholder that the kit swaps as soon as
the page has loaded — once, with no clock, carrying the session and the
headers of the page it sits in.
src is an ordinary route that answers Ctx.Fragment, the same route Poll would
ask, and it must return an element with this id — that is what is being
replaced. Without JavaScript the placeholder carries a link to src, which
answers as a page like any other: the slow part is one click away instead of
missing.
A fragment that fails puts a message and a "try again" in the hole rather
than pulsing for ever, and both sentences are rendered here, in the app's
language, so the behaviour never has to invent text.
Load LiveScript once in the layout — Defer is the same machinery as Poll.
summary: Defer serves the page now and fills this part of it a moment later.
example:
ui.Container(
	ui.Grid(stats...),
	ui.Defer(c, "insights", "/panel/insights", ui.DeferOpts{Height: "12rem"}),
)





see: ui.Poll, ui.LiveScript, ui.Skeleton

name: DropzoneOpts
doc:
DropzoneOpts describes the area. Name is the form field, and it is the name
the route reads with c.Files.
summary: DropzoneOpts describes the area.

fields.name: Accept
fields.doc: Accept and MaxSize are the courtesy check in the browser: they keep the obvious mistake from crossing the network.

fields.name: Single
fields.doc: Single turns off multiple selection; the area takes one file at a time.

name: Dropzone
doc:
Dropzone is an area that takes files by dragging or by clicking, inside the
form that says where they go. With ui.UploadScript on the page the files are
sent one request each — one line of the queue, one progress bar, one message
each — and every answer swaps the element ui.UploadTo names. With the script
off it is an <input type=file multiple> and the form's own button sends them
all at once, which is why the route is written once, against c.Files.

A file the route refuses answers 4xx, and the queue shows the answer's text
on that file's line: the message belongs to the file, not to the form.
summary: Dropzone is an area that takes files by dragging or by clicking, inside the form that says where they go.
example:
h.Form(h.Method("post"), h.Action("/files"), h.EncType("multipart/form-data"),
	ui.UploadTo("list"), trilha.CSRFInput(c),
	ui.Dropzone(ui.DropzoneOpts{Name: "files", Accept: "application/pdf", MaxSize: 50 << 20},
		h.P(h.Text("Drop the PDFs here, or click to choose"))),
	ui.Submit(h.Text("Send")))

name: EmptyOpts
doc: EmptyOpts is what an empty state says. Only Title is required.
summary: EmptyOpts is what an empty state says.

fields.name: Icon
fields.doc: Icon is a name from the kit's set.

fields.name: Title
fields.doc: Title is the sentence in bold: "No documents yet".

fields.name: Hint
fields.doc: Hint is the smaller line under it, and it is the one that earns its place: "Send the first PDF and classification starts on its own" tells somebody what to do, where "no results" only tells them to leave.

fields.name: Action
fields.doc: Action is the way out — a link, a button, a form.

name: Empty
doc:
Empty is the state of a screen with nothing on it: centred icon, a title, a hint and a way out. It exists because the alternative is what every application actually has: one hand-written

per screen, none of them alike, and none of them saying what to do next.
summary: Empty is the state of a screen with nothing on it: centred icon, a title, a hint and a way out.
example:
ui.Empty(ui.EmptyOpts{
	Icon:   "info",
	Title:  "No documents yet",
	Hint:   "Send the first PDF and classification starts on its own.",
	Action: ui.ButtonLink("/upload", h.Text("Send a document")),
})


see: ui.EmptyError, ui.DataTable

name: EmptyError
signature: EmptyError(c *trilha.Ctx, title string, err error, action h.Node) h.Node
doc:
EmptyError is the state of a screen that could not load. The message is what
the person reads; the error itself is shown only in development, because a
stack or a driver's sentence on a production page is an information leak with
a friendly font.
summary: EmptyError is the state of a screen that could not load.

name: FormatOpt
doc: FormatOpt tunes a formatter.
summary: FormatOpt tunes a formatter.

name: Relative
doc:
Relative writes "3 min ago" and keeps the absolute time in the title and in
the datetime attribute.

Nothing here keeps it up to date: the kit has no clock and does not want one.
A screen that needs the number to keep moving puts the piece in a ui.Poll,
which is a decision the page makes and pays for, once.
summary: Relative writes "3 min ago" and keeps the absolute time in the title and in the datetime attribute.

name: DateOnly
doc: DateOnly drops the time of day.
summary: DateOnly drops the time of day.

name: TimeOnly
doc: TimeOnly keeps only the time of day.
summary: TimeOnly keeps only the time of day.

name: Decimals
doc: Decimals fixes how many decimal places a number shows.
summary: Decimals fixes how many decimal places a number shows.

name: Date
doc:
Date renders a moment as <time>, in the app's zone and language.

The zero time and a nil *time.Time render as a dash: a row with no date is a
row with no date, not the first day of year one.
summary: Date renders a moment as <time>, in the app's zone and language.
example:
ui.Date(c, doc.CreatedAt)                // 08/09/2026 12:04
ui.Date(c, doc.CreatedAt, ui.Relative()) // 3 min ago, absolute in the title
ui.Date(c, doc.CreatedAt, ui.DateOnly()) // 08/09/2026


see: ui.Bytes, ui.Duration, ui.Number

name: Bytes
doc:
Bytes renders a size in base 10 — kB, MB, GB — which is what the file manager
of whoever is reading already shows them. The exact number stays in the
title, because "1.4 MB" is the answer to "how big" and not to "how many
bytes".
summary: Bytes renders a size in base 10 — kB, MB, GB — which is what the file manager of whoever is reading already shows them.

name: Duration
doc:
Duration renders an elapsed time the way a person says it: "2 min 13 s",
"1 h 5 min", "340 ms".
summary: Duration renders an elapsed time the way a person says it: "2 min 13 s", "1 h 5 min", "340 ms".

name: Number
doc:
Number renders a count or a measure with the thousands separator of the
language: 12.345 in pt-BR, 12,345 in English.

Money is not here. The currency, where the symbol goes and how a negative
reads are the application's to decide; ui.Number(c, v, ui.Decimals(2)) with
the symbol written beside it is the whole recipe.
summary: Number renders a count or a measure with the thousands separator of the language: 12.345 in pt-BR, 12,345 in English.
example:
ui.Number(c, total)                   // 12,345
ui.Number(c, price, ui.Decimals(2))   // 1,234.56


see: ui.Date, ui.Bytes, ui.Duration

name: Column
doc:
Column is one column of DataTable. Key is the name the URL uses to order by
it, Cell renders the value of one row.
summary: Column is one column of DataTable.

name: Columns
doc: Columns is the columns of a listing, in the order they appear.
summary: Columns is the columns of a listing, in the order they appear.

name: ListSelect
doc:
ListSelect adds a checkbox to each row and a bar with the actions that take
the selection. The form is a POST with the CSRF token, so the action is a
route like any other.
summary: ListSelect adds a checkbox to each row and a bar with the actions that take the selection.

name: ListState
doc:
ListState is the listing minus the rows: where it is, how big it is, what it
shows when it is empty, and which id the fragment swaps.
summary: ListState is the listing minus the rows: where it is, how big it is, what it shows when it is empty, and which id the fragment swaps.

name: DataTable
signature: DataTable[T any](c *trilha.Ctx, cols Columns[T], rows []T, st ListState) h.Node
doc:
DataTable renders the screen every management app has: filter on top, table
in the middle, pagination at the foot, and all of it in the address — a page
that can be shared, reloaded and used with the back button.

With ID set, the ordering links, the filter form and the pagination ask for
the fragment and swap it in place; with JavaScript off the same links and the
same form navigate, and the route answers the whole page. There is no new
script here either way.
A Sort that is not one of the columns marked Sort is dropped before anything
is rendered, and reported in the request's log: the repository never receives
a column name that nobody declared.
summary: DataTable renders the screen every management app has: filter on top, table in the middle, pagination at the foot, and all of it in the address — a page that can be shared, reloaded and used with the back button.

name: Poll
doc:
Poll asks the route for this fragment again every so often, and swaps it —
the screen of a job that runs on the server without anybody clicking. The
element needs an id: it is the id the fragment is asked for.

The interval is "6s", "500ms" or "2m". src is where to ask; the address of
the page itself when it is empty. The client pauses while the tab is hidden
and asks again as soon as it comes back, backs off to a minute after an
error and returns to the interval on the first answer, and obeys what the
route says: Ctx.PollStop ends it, Ctx.PollEvery changes the rhythm.
The first render of the fragment is already on the page, so a visitor with
no JavaScript sees the state as it was when the page loaded — old, never
broken. Load the behavior with LiveScript.
summary: Poll asks the route for this fragment again every so often, and swaps it — the screen of a job that runs on the server without anybody clicking.
example: h.Div(h.ID("status"), ui.Poll("6s", "/docs/42/status"), status(doc))

name: Live
doc:
Live opens one Server-Sent Events connection for the page, to the route that
says what changed. Put it once, in the layout or at the top of the page:

The connection carries names, never HTML: each name wakes up the fragments
marked with On, which ask their route again. The route is an ordinary GET
that calls Ctx.Stream and Stream.Notify.
summary: Live opens one Server-Sent Events connection for the page, to the route that says what changed.
example: h.Body(ui.Live("/events"), ...)

name: On
doc:
On swaps this fragment when the stream announces that name. The element
needs an id, like Poll, and Poll is the fallback: a fragment with both waits
for the event while the connection is up and goes back to the clock when it
is down.
summary: On swaps this fragment when the stream announces that name.
example: h.Div(h.ID("status"), ui.On("doc:42", "/docs/42/status"), ui.Poll("30s", ""), status(doc))

name: LiveScript
doc:
LiveScript loads ui.live.js, the behavior behind Poll, Live and On. Put it
once, in the layout of the area that uses them — the kit's Head does not
load it, so a page with nothing to watch does not download it.
summary: LiveScript loads ui.live.js, the behavior behind Poll, Live and On.

name: MarkdownOpts
doc:
MarkdownOpts tunes Markdown. The zero value is the safe one: headings
demoted to <h3>, no images, no raw HTML.
summary: MarkdownOpts tunes Markdown.

fields.name: HeadingBase
fields.doc: HeadingBase is the level a single "#" becomes.

fields.name: Images
fields.doc: Images turns ![alt](url) into an .

fields.name: Class
fields.doc: Class is added to the wrapping <div>, on top of "ui-md".

name: Markdown
doc:
Markdown renders a subset of CommonMark as a tree of nodes: paragraphs,
headings, lists, blockquotes, fenced and inline code, GFM tables, links,
emphasis and hard breaks.

It is written for text that came from a language model or from a person, so
the rule that matters is the one with no exception: there is no raw HTML.
A tag in the source is text in the output, because the output is a tree the
h package escapes by construction — never a string somebody could hand to
h.Raw.
summary: Markdown renders a subset of CommonMark as a tree of nodes: paragraphs, headings, lists, blockquotes, fenced and inline code, GFM tables, links, emphasis and hard breaks.
example: ui.Markdown(answer, ui.MarkdownOpts{})

name: Policy
doc:
Policy is what PolicyGrid needs to draw a permission matrix: the columns, the
values a cell may hold, the rows, and what is in each cell.

It is an interface and not auth.Policy because the kit must not drag
authentication into an application that only draws buttons. auth.Policy
satisfies it as it is.
summary: Policy is what PolicyGrid needs to draw a permission matrix: the columns, the values a cell may hold, the rows, and what is in each cell.

name: PolicyGridOpts
doc: PolicyGridOpts configures the grid.
summary: PolicyGridOpts configures the grid.

fields.name: Action
fields.doc: Action is where the form posts.

fields.name: Labels
fields.doc: Labels renames a module for the screen: the code says "docs", the person reading says "Documents".

fields.name: None
fields.doc: None is what the empty option says.

fields.name: Submit
fields.doc: Submit is the button's text.

fields.name: ReadOnly
fields.doc: ReadOnly draws the same grid with every control disabled, which is what somebody who may see the matrix but not change it should get.

fields.name: CSRF
fields.doc: CSRF is the hidden token field, and a form that changes permissions has to carry one: pass trilha.CSRFInput(c).

name: PolicyGrid
doc:
PolicyGrid renders the permission matrix as a form: one row per role, one
column per module, a select of levels in each cell.

The fields are named grant.<role>.<module>, which is what auth.BindPolicy
reads on the other side. There is no JavaScript: it is a form, it posts, the
handler saves and redirects.
Whoever draws this screen has to guard it — a grid that edits the matrix is
the most valuable screen in the application, and it must sit behind the
module that administers it.
summary: PolicyGrid renders the permission matrix as a form: one row per role, one column per module, a select of levels in each cell.
example: ui.PolicyGrid(acesso.Policy, ui.PolicyGridOpts{Action: "/admin/permissoes"})

the fields and nothing else — the <form>, the CSRF input and the button are
the app's, as in every other form of the kit, because where the form posts
and what the button says are not in the schema.

values and errs are what BindSchema returned, so a form that came back with
messages comes back filled in.
summary: SchemaForm renders a form the product defined at runtime: the step of a workflow, the public form behind a token, the settings of a tenant.

errs, _ := err.(trilha.FieldErrors)

name: SecretField
signature: SecretField(c *trilha.Ctx, name, label string, current trilha.Secret, opts ...FieldOpt) h.Node
doc:
SecretField is the input for a value that must never come back whole: an API
key, a webhook secret, an SMTP password.

It draws an empty password field and, under it, what is stored — masked —
plus the sentence that makes the whole thing work: leave it blank to keep
what is there. That is not decoration. A form has no way to send
"unchanged", so a screen that pre-fills the field either sends the secret
back to the browser (where the DevTools show it) or wipes it on the first
save that somebody did not retype. trilha.Secret and Bind already agree on
this: an empty value leaves the stored one alone.
summary: SecretField is the input for a value that must never come back whole: an API key, a webhook secret, an SMTP password.
example:
ui.SecretField(c, "token", "Provider token", cfg.Token)


see: trilha.Secret, trilha.Seal

theme before the first paint, so the sidebar does not open and close in front
of whoever asked for it closed. On a narrow screen the same class is what
slides the drawer.

name: Steps
doc:
Steps is the indicator of a form in several screens: where somebody is, what
is behind them, and what is left.

current is 1-based and is the step being filled. Behind it the steps are
links (they were done, and going back is normal); ahead of it they are
plain text. The current one carries aria-current="step", which is how a
screen reader says "you are here" in a list of five.
It draws the indicator and nothing else: the state between one screen and
the next is trilha.Ctx.Draft, and the form is yours.
summary: Steps is the indicator of a form in several screens: where somebody is, what is behind them, and what is left.

	{Label: "File", Href: "/import/1"},
	{Label: "Mapping", Href: "/import/2"},

name: TaskProgress
doc:
TaskProgress is the bar that watches one task: the step, how far along, and
the failure when there was one.

It is a Poll that stops on its own: while the task is alive the fragment
asks again every two seconds, and the moment it finishes the route answers
Ctx.PollStop and the browser stops asking. Without JavaScript it is the
state as of when the page loaded — old, never broken — and reloading is the
refresh.
The id comes from the application, which knows which task belongs to the
screen; passing one the visitor sent would be letting them watch somebody
else's work.
summary: TaskProgress is the bar that watches one task: the step, how far along, and the failure when there was one.

name: Tree
doc:
Tree renders a hierarchy that opens node by node.

Each node is a <details>, so it opens with no JavaScript at all; what the
script adds is fetching the children the first time instead of asking the
server for a whole page. A node whose children are already in Nodes never
asks for anything, which is why the path down to Current arrives open and
complete on the first render.
The roles are the real ones — tree, treeitem, group, aria-expanded — and the
arrows, Home, End and "*" move through it. Load TreeScript once on the page.
summary: Tree renders a hierarchy that opens node by node.

name: TreeNodes
signature: TreeNodes[T any](items []T, of func(T) TreeNode) h.Node
doc:

because the browser has nothing to decide about them.
summary: TreeNodes is what a source route answers: the children of one node, as HTML, because the browser has nothing to decide about them.

doc:

doc:

one value that posts.
summary: TreePickerOpts is the field: a search that finds, a tree that browses, and one value that posts.

fields.name: Name
fields.doc: Name is what the form posts — a radio per node, so choosing is a form control and not a script.

fields.name: Value
fields.doc: Value is what is already chosen.

fields.name: Nodes
fields.doc: Nodes are the roots (with the path down to Value already open).

fields.name: Source
fields.doc: Source answers the children of ?parent=<value>.

fields.name: Search
fields.doc: Search answers TreeNodes for ?q=, flattened, each with its Path — the match of a code deep in the tree only means something with its ancestry beside it.

fields.name: Placeholder
fields.doc: Placeholder and Label are the search field's text and the tree's accessible name.

fields.name: MinChars
fields.doc: MinChars is how much has to be typed before searching (2 when zero).

name: TreePicker
doc:
TreePicker is choosing one node out of thousands: type to find it, or browse
to it.

The value posts as a radio, which is the whole no-JavaScript story: a person
with no script browses the same <details> and picks the same radio, and the
form posts the same field. The search box then behaves like any filter — it
submits, and the route renders the picker with the matches.
With the script, typing asks Search and puts the matches in place of the
tree, each with the ancestry it came from; clearing the box brings the tree
back.
summary: TreePicker is choosing one node out of thousands: type to find it, or browse to it.
example:
ui.Field("code", "Classification", ui.TreePicker(ui.TreePickerOpts{
	Name:   "code",
	Value:  form.Code,
	Nodes:  plan.Roots(form.Code), // open down to what is chosen
	Source: "/classification/nodes",
	Search: "/classification/search",
}))

name: TreeScript
doc:

one does not download it.
summary: TreeScript loads ui.tree.js, the behaviour behind Tree and TreePicker: the children fetched on the first open, the search, and the keyboard.

signature: CheckRow(control h.Node, label string, forID string) h.Node
doc:
CheckRow puts a checkbox/switch/radio beside its label. forID is the
control's id: without it the label is decoration and the click area is the
box alone.
summary: CheckRow puts a checkbox/switch/radio beside its label.
example: ui.CheckRow(ui.Checkbox(h.ID("terms"), h.Name("terms")), "I agree", "terms")

name: Field
signature: Field(id, label string, control h.Node, opts ...FieldOpt) h.Node
doc:
Field is label + control + optional help/error. id must match the control's id.
An error marks the control invalid via aria-describedby on the wrapper.
summary: Field is label + control + optional help/error.
example:
ui.Field("email", "E-mail",
	ui.Input(h.ID("email"), h.Type("email"), h.Name("email"), ui.InvalidIf(errs, "email")),
	ui.Errors(errs, "email"))

name: FieldOpt
doc: FieldOpt configures Field.
summary: FieldOpt configures Field.

name: Help
doc:
Help, Error, Errors and With are the FieldOpt options: a hint under the
control, one message, the messages a FieldErrors carries for that name, and
anything else to put inside the field.
summary: Help, Error, Errors and With are the FieldOpt options: a hint under the control, one message, the messages a FieldErrors carries for that name, and anything else to put inside the field.

Help, Error, Errors and With are the FieldOpt options: a hint under the
control, one message, the messages a FieldErrors carries for that name, and
anything else to put inside the field.

name: With
doc: With adds attributes to the field wrapper (e.g. ShowWhen).
summary: With adds attributes to the field wrapper (e.g.

name: Invalid
doc:
Invalid marks a control invalid (red ring). Pass it to Input/Select when
there is an error for the field.
summary: Invalid marks a control invalid (red ring).

name: Navigate
doc:
Navigate marks a region whose links navigate on the client: a click on a
same-origin link inside it fetches the next page and replaces the element
with the given id, instead of reloading the document. An empty id means the
marked element is itself the one to replace:

It is off until the region is marked and NavigateScript is on the page, and
it never changes what the server answers: the address in the bar is the one
a normal navigation would use, and reloading it renders the same page.
summary: Navigate marks a region whose links navigate on the client: a click on a same-origin link inside it fetches the next page and replaces the element with the given id, instead of reloading the document.
example: h.Main(h.ID("conteudo"), ui.Navigate(""), children)

name: NoNavigate
doc:
NoNavigate keeps one link out of it (a download, another app, a route that
must reload for real), inside a region marked with Navigate.
summary: NoNavigate keeps one link out of it (a download, another app, a route that must reload for real), inside a region marked with Navigate.

name: NavigateScript
doc:
NavigateScript loads ui.nav.js, the behavior behind Navigate. Put it once,
in the layout of the area that uses it — the kit's Head does not load it, so
an app without client navigation does not download it.
summary: NavigateScript loads ui.nav.js, the behavior behind Navigate.

name: UploadTo
doc:
UploadTo marks a form that sends a file: the kit sends it with XHR, shows how
much has gone out and swaps element id with what comes back — the same
fragment the route already answers. Without JavaScript the form submits
normally and the route answers the whole page.

It is a different attribute from Swap on purpose: a form carrying both would
be sent twice.
summary: UploadTo marks a form that sends a file: the kit sends it with XHR, shows how much has gone out and swaps element id with what comes back — the same fragment the route already answers.
example:
h.Form(h.Method("post"), h.Action("/anexos"), h.EncType("multipart/form-data"),
	ui.UploadTo("lista"), trilha.CSRFInput(c),
	ui.Input(h.Type("file"), h.Name("arquivo")), ui.UploadBar(),
	ui.Submit(h.Text("Send")))

name: UploadBar
doc:
UploadBar is the progress element UploadTo fills in. It starts hidden and is
only shown while sending; style it through the progress selector.
summary: UploadBar is the progress element UploadTo fills in.

name: UploadScript
doc:
UploadScript loads ui.upload.js, the behavior behind UploadTo. Put it once,
in the layout or page that has the form; ui.Head does not load it.
summary: UploadScript loads ui.upload.js, the behavior behind UploadTo.

name: Swap
doc:
Swap marks a link or form as a fragment request: clicking or submitting it
asks the same route for the part of the page with the given id and replaces
that element, without reloading.

With JavaScript off nothing here applies: the link navigates and the form
submits as usual, and the route answers with the whole page. On the server,
Ctx.Fragment reports the requested id.
summary: Swap marks a link or form as a fragment request: clicking or submitting it asks the same route for the part of the page with the given id and replaces that element, without reloading.
example:
h.Form(h.Method("get"), ui.Swap("lista"), busca())
h.Div(h.ID("lista"), ...)

name: Indicator
doc:
Indicator marks an element as the pending signal for the target with the
given id: it stays hidden while nothing is happening and appears once the
request for that target has been in flight past the threshold. Put it
anywhere — beside the target, in the header, inside the button.

The threshold is what keeps a fast answer from making it blink; see
PendingAfter. Several indicators may watch the same target.
summary: Indicator marks an element as the pending signal for the target with the given id: it stays hidden while nothing is happening and appears once the request for that target has been in flight past the threshold.
example: ui.Spinner(ui.Indicator("lista"))

name: PendingAfter
doc:
PendingAfter sets, in milliseconds, how long a request may be in flight
before the page says so. Put it on the element that carries Swap or on the
one that carries Navigate. The default is 120 ms, which is about where a
person starts to notice a wait; zero or less means the default.

The threshold is the whole point: showing a spinner for the 40 ms answer is
the flash people complain about, not a courtesy.
summary: PendingAfter sets, in milliseconds, how long a request may be in flight before the page says so.

name: NoTransition
doc:
NoTransition turns off the crossfade a swap or a navigation would animate on
this trigger. The transition already does nothing where the browser has no
startViewTransition and where the system asks for less motion, so this is for
the page that wants the instant replacement on purpose.
summary: NoTransition turns off the crossfade a swap or a navigation would animate on this trigger.

name: Spinner
doc:
Spinner is a turning ring, sized by the font it sits in. It is decorative —
the waiting is announced by aria-busy on the target — so it is hidden from
assistive technology.
summary: Spinner is a turning ring, sized by the font it sits in.

name: NoPush
doc: NoPush turns off the history entry a fragment link would create.
summary: NoPush turns off the history entry a fragment link would create.

name: ShowWhen
doc:
ShowWhen shows the element only while the named form field has one of the
given values ("a|b"); with no values, while the field is non-empty. Hidden
groups have their controls disabled, so they are not submitted.
summary: ShowWhen shows the element only while the named form field has one of the given values ("a|b"); with no values, while the field is non-empty.

name: Badge
doc: Badge is a small label for a status; the variants apply.
summary: Badge is a small label for a status; the variants apply.
example: ui.Badge(ui.Secondary(), h.Text("draft"))

name: Alert
doc: Alert renders a titled notice; add Destructive() for errors and an Icon first.
summary: Alert renders a titled notice; add Destructive() for errors and an Icon first.

name: AlertDescription
doc: AlertDescription is the body of an Alert.
summary: AlertDescription is the body of an Alert.

name: Toaster
doc: Toaster is the container toasts stack into; place it once in the layout.
summary: Toaster is the container toasts stack into; place it once in the layout.

name: Toast
signature: Toast(kind, text string, fadeMs int) h.Node
doc:
Toast is a message that fades out after fadeMs (0 = stays). kind: "",
"success" or "error". Render it inside Toaster (e.g. after a form post).
summary: Toast is a message that fades out after fadeMs (0 = stays).
example: ui.Toaster(ui.Toast("success", "Invoice sent.", 4000))

name: Flashes
doc:
Flashes renders the messages left by c.Flash on the request before, inside
the toaster. It replaces Toaster() in the layout:

An empty toaster is still rendered, because ui.js appends live toasts to it.
summary: Flashes renders the messages left by c.Flash on the request before, inside the toaster.
example: h.Body(..., ui.Flashes(c))

name: Confirm
doc:
Confirm asks before the form it sits in is submitted. Put it in the form,
next to the CSRF input:

ui.js holds the submit, opens the kit's dialog and only then lets it
through, fragment forms included. The confirming button repeats the label of
the button that was pressed; the other one says "Cancel", or whatever
h.Data("ui-confirm-cancel", "…") says on the same form. Without JavaScript
the form submits straight away — when that is not good enough, ask on a page
of its own, which works either way.
summary: Confirm asks before the form it sits in is submitted.
example:
h.Form(h.Method("post"), h.Action("/blog/"+p.Slug), trilha.CSRFInput(c),
	ui.Confirm("Delete this post?", "There is no undo."),
	ui.Submit(Destructive(), h.Text("Delete")))

name: Table
doc: Table wraps a <table class="ui-table"> in a horizontally scrollable box.
summary: Table wraps a <table class="ui-table"> in a horizontally scrollable box.

name: Num
doc: Num right-aligns numeric cells.
summary: Num right-aligns numeric cells.

name: Depth
doc: Depth indents the first cell of a row (tree tables, drill-down).
summary: Depth indents the first cell of a row (tree tables, drill-down).

name: Tab
doc: Tab is one tab of Tabs.
summary: Tab is one tab of Tabs.

name: Tabs
doc: Tabs renders an accessible tab list; the first tab starts selected.
summary: Tabs renders an accessible tab list; the first tab starts selected.

name: Dialog
doc: Dialog renders a native <dialog>; open it with DialogTrigger(id, ...).
summary: Dialog renders a native <dialog>; open it with DialogTrigger(id, ...).
example:
ui.DialogTrigger("confirm", h.Text("Delete"))
ui.Dialog("confirm", "Delete the invoice?",
	ui.DialogDescription("This cannot be undone."),
	ui.DialogFooter(ui.DialogClose(ui.Outline(), h.Text("Cancel")), deleteForm))

name: DialogDescription
doc:
DialogDescription is the line under a Dialog title, and DialogFooter is the
row of buttons at the bottom.
summary: DialogDescription is the line under a Dialog title, and DialogFooter is the row of buttons at the bottom.

name: DialogFooter
doc:
DialogDescription is the line under a Dialog title, and DialogFooter is the
row of buttons at the bottom.
summary: DialogDescription is the line under a Dialog title, and DialogFooter is the row of buttons at the bottom.

name: DialogTrigger
doc: DialogTrigger is a Button that opens the dialog with the given id.
summary: DialogTrigger is a Button that opens the dialog with the given id.

name: DialogClose
doc: DialogClose is a Button that closes the enclosing dialog.
summary: DialogClose is a Button that closes the enclosing dialog.

name: MenuTrigger
doc: MenuTrigger toggles the popover menu with the given id.
summary: MenuTrigger toggles the popover menu with the given id.

name: Menu
doc: Menu is a popover list of MenuItem/MenuLink.
summary: Menu is a popover list of MenuItem/MenuLink.

name: MenuItem
doc:
MenuItem is an entry that does something (a button) and MenuLink is one that
goes somewhere (a link). Both belong inside a Menu.
summary: MenuItem is an entry that does something (a button) and MenuLink is one that goes somewhere (a link).

name: MenuLink
doc:
MenuItem is an entry that does something (a button) and MenuLink is one that
goes somewhere (a link). Both belong inside a Menu.
summary: MenuItem is an entry that does something (a button) and MenuLink is one that goes somewhere (a link).

name: Separator
doc: Separator is a horizontal rule between sections.
summary: Separator is a horizontal rule between sections.

name: Skeleton
doc: Skeleton is a loading placeholder; pass StyleAttr for size.
summary: Skeleton is a loading placeholder; pass StyleAttr for size.

name: Progress
doc: Progress renders a bar at value/max.
summary: Progress renders a bar at value/max.

name: Crumb
doc: Crumb is one breadcrumb item; the last one is the current page.
summary: Crumb is one breadcrumb item; the last one is the current page.

name: Breadcrumb
doc: Breadcrumb renders a navigation trail.
summary: Breadcrumb renders a navigation trail.

name: Pages
doc: Pages describes the page navigation Pagination renders.
summary: Pages describes the page navigation Pagination renders.

name: Pagination
doc:
Pagination renders page navigation as real links, so a page can be shared,
reloaded and indexed. The current page is a <span> with aria-current: it is
where the visitor already is, and a link to here is a link to nowhere. The
edges are not disabled links either — the first page has no previous, so
nothing is rendered for it. A list with one page renders nothing at all.

The window keeps the first and last page and the ones around the current
one, with an ellipsis over each gap, so the footer does not grow with the
table.
summary: Pagination renders page navigation as real links, so a page can be shared, reloaded and indexed.

name: Tooltip
doc:
Tooltip attaches a hint to what it wraps. The text is in title, so the hint
works with ui.js off — that is the browser's own tooltip. With the script on
the page, title is removed (two tooltips is worse than none), a bubble with
role=tooltip takes its place and the target gets aria-describedby, so the
hint is reachable by keyboard focus and by touch, and closes with Escape.

The text is a string on purpose: a hint with a link inside is a popover, and
that is what Menu is for.
summary: Tooltip attaches a hint to what it wraps.

name: Avatar
doc: Avatar shows an image or the initials as fallback.
summary: Avatar shows an image or the initials as fallback.

name: Collapsible
doc: Collapsible is a <details> with a styled summary; pass h.Open() to start open.
summary: Collapsible is a <details> with a styled summary; pass h.Open() to start open.

name: ThemeToggle
doc: ThemeToggle switches light/dark and remembers the choice.
summary: ThemeToggle switches light/dark and remembers the choice.

name: Icon
doc:
Icon renders an embedded Lucide icon (ISC). It panics on unknown names,
which is a programming error caught at first render. See Icons.
summary: Icon renders an embedded Lucide icon (ISC).

name: Icons
doc: Icons lists the available icon names.
summary: Icons lists the available icon names.

name: Errors
doc:
Errors is a Field option that shows the message for field from errs (a
trilha.FieldErrors or any map); no-op when the field has no error.
summary: Errors is a Field option that shows the message for field from errs (a trilha.FieldErrors or any map); no-op when the field has no error.

name: InvalidIf
doc: InvalidIf marks a control invalid when errs has a message for field.
summary: InvalidIf marks a control invalid when errs has a message for field.

name: Option
doc: Option is one <option> of SelectOptions.
summary: Option is one <option> of SelectOptions.

name: SelectOptions
doc:
SelectOptions renders <option>s, marking the one equal to selected. A
leading placeholder can be given as Option{"", "Escolha…"}.
summary: SelectOptions renders <option>s, marking the one equal to selected.

name: Checked
doc: Checked returns h.Checked() when v is true (checkbox/switch round-trips).
summary: Checked returns h.Checked() when v is true (checkbox/switch round-trips).

name: Status
doc:
Status renders the badge of an enum value: the label a person reads, in the
tone the enum declared.

A value the enum does not know renders raw, in the muted tone: a row written
before somebody retired that value must not take the screen down.
summary: Status renders the badge of an enum value: the label a person reads, in the tone the enum declared.
example: ui.Status(docs.Status, doc.Status) // Processed see: trilha.Enum, ui.Badge
